title: Legacy stale full-matrix lock can deny scheduler service
security_invariant: The scheduler opens a regular non-symlink .full-matrix-run.lock below private MATRIX_ROOT on FD 9, acquires flock -n 9, and holds that FD for the full scheduler lifetime. Running job/Make descendants inherit FD 9, so SIGKILL of only the scheduler parent intentionally leaves the lock active until the final descendant exits; the kernel then releases it and the same lock path can be reused. A competing scheduler must not enter while any live holder retains FD 9; no secondary control path or release interface exists.
trust_boundary: The private MATRIX_ROOT filesystem boundary and the kernel-held FD 9 lock distinguish the running scheduler and its job/Make descendants from a competing process. A regular non-symlink lock file and inherited shell-held descriptor preserve the ownership boundary without durable ownership state or a secondary release interface.
sink: Full-matrix scheduler admission; an incorrect lock protocol can either deny service after owner death or allow a competing scheduler to impersonate release and overlap a live owner.
observed_behavior: The prior mkdir-based full-matrix lock directory remained after its owner received SIGKILL. A later scheduler treated that orphaned directory as live and could be denied service indefinitely. A final release-impersonation review superseded the interim helper design entirely. The final local implementation in ci/runtime/lifecycle/run-full-matrix-parallel.sh opens a regular non-symlink .full-matrix-run.lock under private MATRIX_ROOT on shell FD 9, takes flock -n 9, and holds that descriptor for the whole scheduler. Running job/Make descendants inherit FD 9, so SIGKILL of only the scheduler parent leaves the lock active until the final descendant exits; the kernel then releases it for reuse on the same lock path. No secondary ownership state or release interface exists. The parent-confirmed local scheduler suite reported eight passing tests with -W error::ResourceWarning, including test_scheduler_rejects_a_live_full_matrix_lock_owner and test_scheduler_lock_outlives_a_sigkilled_parent_until_its_job_descendant_exits. Hosted exact-successor evidence is still pending.
expected_behavior: A live scheduler holds FD 9 and flock -n 9 for its entire lifetime, so a competing scheduler receives the normal busy result and cannot release, replace, or bypass it. Running job/Make descendants inherit the descriptor; SIGKILL of only the scheduler parent must retain the advisory lock until the final descendant exits, after which kernel cleanup permits reuse of the same regular non-symlink lock path within private MATRIX_ROOT. No secondary ownership state or release interface exists.
impact: The legacy persistent mkdir lock could deny later full-matrix runs and invalidate release evidence after an owner died. A release helper or owner-record recovery path could also permit release impersonation against a live owner. The final shell-held kernel lock removes both paths, but this validated P1 availability/security boundary remains a release blocker until hosted exact-successor evidence is available.
preconditions: A full-matrix scheduler acquires the legacy mkdir lock
The owner is terminated with SIGKILL before legacy cleanup removes the lock directory
A later full-matrix scheduler attempts admission through the same lock path
reproduction: Start a full-matrix scheduler using the prior mkdir-based lock implementation.
Terminate its owner with SIGKILL before cleanup.
Start a second scheduler and observe that the persistent directory blocks admission although no owner remains.

Run the scheduler regression suite and confirm that a live FD 9 owner blocks a competitor, then SIGKILL of only the scheduler parent leaves the lock active until its final job/Make descendant exits and the same path is reusable.

evidence.artifact_type: parent-supplied final security review and local scheduler-test outcome
evidence.result: Parent-confirmed: 8 scheduler tests passed with ResourceWarning treated as an error, including test_scheduler_rejects_a_live_full_matrix_lock_owner and test_scheduler_lock_outlives_a_sigkilled_parent_until_its_job_descendant_exits.

root_cause: A durable mkdir lock directory remained after SIGKILL and was treated as proof of a live owner. The release-impersonation review also established that a separate lock-control path would add an avoidable authority boundary against a live scheduler.
proposed_remediation: The final local correction in ci/runtime/lifecycle/run-full-matrix-parallel.sh opens a regular non-symlink .full-matrix-run.lock under private MATRIX_ROOT on shell FD 9, acquires flock -n 9, and holds that FD for the scheduler lifetime. Running job/Make descendants inherit FD 9; SIGKILL of only the scheduler parent leaves the lock active until the final descendant exits, when kernel cleanup releases it for reuse. Preserve the single FD 9 ownership path and absence of a release interface; retain the eight focused scheduler controls and obtain final exact-successor hosted validation.
acceptance_criteria: A live scheduler holding FD 9 and flock -n 9 rejects a competing scheduler without release, replacement, or bypass.

SIGKILL of only the scheduler parent leaves the kernel lock active while a job/Make descendant retains inherited FD 9; after the final descendant exits, kernel cleanup releases it and a later scheduler can acquire the same path.
The lock file is regular and non-symlink below private MATRIX_ROOT.
Only the shell-held FD 9 ownership path remains; no secondary control path or release interface exists.
All eight tests in tests.test_full_matrix_parallel_scheduler, including the named live-owner and SIGKILL regressions, pass.
A fresh hosted exact-successor run confirms the lock behavior without weakening scheduler isolation or result policy.
validation_plan: Re-run PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -W error::ResourceWarning -m unittest -v tests.test_full_matrix_parallel_scheduler and retain an exact local receipt.
Exercise live-owner contention and prove that SIGKILL of only the scheduler parent preserves the lock until the final inherited job/Make descendant exits, then permits reuse of the same path.
Obtain fresh hosted exact-successor full-matrix, producer, review, and protected-integration evidence before fixed or verified status.
legitimate_control_tests: A live scheduler holds FD 9 and a competing scheduler receives the expected busy result.
Closing the final copy of FD 9 releases its kernel lock without a secondary release operation.
SIGKILL of only the scheduler parent leaves the lock held by an inherited job/Make descriptor; after the final descendant exits, a subsequent scheduler acquires the same path normally.

history.detail: Parent final security review confirmed that the prior mkdir lock survives SIGKILL and can deny later scheduler service. The final implementation is recorded separately in the superseding release-impersonation review event; hosted exact-successor evidence remains required.

Release-impersonation review retained only the shell-held FD 9 ownership path. Final implementation holds flock -n 9 on a regular non-symlink .full-matrix-run.lock below private MATRIX_ROOT for the full scheduler lifetime; closing the final descriptor releases the lock. The later correction records that SIGKILL of only the scheduler parent retains the inherited-descriptor lock until the final job/Make descendant exits. Parent reported eight passing scheduler tests with ResourceWarning treated as errors, including the named live-owner and SIGKILL controls.

Parent clarified that running job/Make descendants inherit FD 9. SIGKILL of only the scheduler parent therefore intentionally leaves flock active until the last descendant exits; only then does kernel cleanup release the lock for reuse on the same path. The regression name is test_scheduler_lock_outlives_a_sigkilled_parent_until_its_job_descendant_exits.
